review_notes:
I read the whole file (lines 1–286) and judged it only against the repeated-proof-machinery rubric. I did not open any related source files.

The main repetition is the eight lemmas `transpose_first_left/right/bottom/top` and `transpose_second_left/right/bottom/top`. Each is a one-line `simpa only [GridRectangleBetween.transpose_*] using congrArg (fun p => p.2.field) D.transpose_first` (or `_second`). This is routine projection unfolding over a sigma-pair equation, not nontrivial mathematical reasoning. A shared lemma would save little and would not make the file easier to read or maintain. It would also probably need extra dependent-type plumbing.

The same applies to the other candidates:
- `isEmpty_transpose_first` and `isEmpty_transpose_second` are thin parallel wrappers around existing API.
- In `ext`, the two `GridRectangleBetween.ext` + `subst` blocks are routine.
- The two bullets at the end of `sides_of_middle_eq_swapRows` are short `rw`/`exact` steps.
- In `target_mem_twoStepColumnSwapNeighbors`, the two `mem_columnSwapNeighbors` witnesses are short applications of existing lemmas.

The rubric calls this kind of repetition insufficient, so I report no finding. The only remaining uncertainty is that I did not check whether the transpose projection lemmas could be proved by `rfl` or generated more compactly. That would be a style improvement, not a case of repeated mathematical reasoning.
